messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: tooltips in svg images
parts:
Hi all,

Does anyone know if it is possible to attach tooltips to ggplot
graphics saved in svg format? There is an R package called
RSVGTipsDevice that does this with base graphics, but I'm not sure how
(or if) it can be made to work properly with ggplot2. Consider the
following example:

library(RSVGTipsDevice) # you probably need to do
install.packages("RSVGTipsDevice") first
library(ggplot2)
data(diamonds)
Di <- diamonds[sample(1:dim(diamonds)[1], 100),]
devSVGTips("TestSVG4.svg", toolTipMode=1,
title="SVG example plot 1")
p <- qplot(depth, price, data=Di)
setSVGShapeToolTip(title="Price", desc="Diamond price is the cost of
the diamond.")
p + scale_y_continuous("Diamond price")
dev.off()

The above example kind of works; a tooltip is written into the svg
file, but it appears to be attached to the plot background rather than
to the y axis label. Does anyone have an idea about how to make this
work? Any other ways I might attach a tooltip to the axis labels? I
know there are some packages for dynamic graphs (playwith for example)
that can do this sort of thing, but I need to put the resulting image
on a webpage, so I think I need an svg-based solution (though I'll be
perfectly happy to hear other ideas).

Thanks for any advice,
Ista

--
Ista Zahn
Graduate student
University of Rochester
Department of Clinical and Social Psychology

messages.subject: Re: tooltips in svg images
parts:
Hi,

I thought that the gridSVG device might help you, but for some reason
it doesn't seem to work with ggplot2. This minimal example results in
an invalid SVG file :(

library(gridSVG)
library(ggplot2)
x11(width=6, height=6)
p = qplot(1, 1)
# print(p)
grid.draw(ggplotGrob(p))
gridToSVG()
dev.off()

gridSVG is tagged "experimental", still Paul Murrell might like to
know about this particular issue.


baptiste

messages.author: a5be32bcb3d808db
messages.subject: Re: tooltips in svg images
parts:
Thanks Baptiste. I took a look at it, but I'm scared off by the
"HIGHLY experimental" description. For those who might find this
information useful in the future, I'll summarize my "progress" on this
issue so far.

My major goal is to present web graphics with limited interactivity,
i.e., hovering over the axis labels should pop up a tool tip
describing the variable mapped to that axis. First I tried
RSVGTipsDevice, but I don't think it can easily be made to work with
ggplot. Next I triedSVGAnnotate, but that does not seem to be working
with my system (OpenSuse 11.2, R 2.10.1). Similarly, gridSVG looks
promising but is highly experimental and is not writing valid svg
output.

So at this point I think I'm going to abandon the svg approach
entirely. It would be nice if it worked, but it just seems too
unstable. My plan as of now is to accomplish my goal by floating empty
html divs with title attributes over .png images. It will take some
work to get this working, as the faceting and size of the images
depend on user input, making it challenging to determine where the
empty div elements should be placed. But honestly I think this is the
easiest and most robust solution.

-Ista
